title: Justice Shehu Ibrahim Ahmad is a prominent figure in the Nigerian judiciary, particularly known for his contributions to the legal profession in Northern Nigeria, where he integrates moral values and Islamic laws. Born in Zaria, Kaduna State in 1958, he began his education in Islamic studies and later pursued a law degree at Bayero University, Kano. After being called to the Nigerian Bar in 1986, he climbed the ranks in the Kano State judiciary, eventually becoming a magistrate and later a Chief Registrar at the Sharia Court of Appeal in Kaduna. His dedication and hard work led to his current position as Kadi of the Kaduna State Sharia Court of Appeal since 2003. Justice Shehu has authored several publications on Sharia law and has participated in numerous legal conferences. He is also a family man, happily married with children.
